CRYPTO NEWS — August 23, 2026

Profit-taking is real. After a screaming 20%+ rally last week, Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana all dropped 2–2.3% overnight despite still sitting in greed territory. Total market cap contracted 5.23%, a sign that traders are cashing out wins and rotation back to BTC is underway. Fear & Greed eased from 71 to 66—still greedy, but the momentum is cooling. This is textbook pullback behavior after a sustained run; the absence of extreme leverage (funding rates flat at 0.0100% across the board) tells you the market isn't overextended, just tired.

TODAY'S HIGHLIGHTS

Bitcoin Miners Get a Lifeline as Hashprice Explodes 20% Higher
Mining profitability just spiked, a direct shot of dopamine to the sector after months of margin pressure. When hashprice jumps like this, it signals renewed conviction in BTC's value by the people with the highest operational stakes. For traders, this is a macro vote of confidence—miners don't blow capex on expansion if they think the cycle is fizzling. Watch whether hashrate jumps in the coming weeks; sustained miner activity often precedes retail FOMO.

Bitcoin and Ether ETFs Draw $2.6 Billion in Strongest Inflow Week Since October, Tripling Volume
Institutional money isn't hesitating. This is the kind of capital flow that typically backstops pullbacks and validates longer-term trends. The volume tripling tells you conviction is real, not just a flash. What this means: dips into support (BTC's $75,775 24h low) become buying opportunities for the smart money. Don't panic-sell on days like today when the macro bid is this strong.

Bitcoin's $100K Forecast May Be Too Low After Record Short Squeeze
Short liquidations have been brutal, and when bears get wiped out at scale, bulls get a cleaner path higher. The leverage destruction removes a structural ceiling that normally caps rallies. For your trading: don't fight the squeeze. Position sizing matters more than direction when shorts are this crowded—one wrong move and stops cascade.

EU Carbon Taxes Push Bitcoin Mining to Russia, Study Claims
Regulatory friction is pushing hash rate east, a slow-burn geopolitical shift that matters for decentralization narratives and future regulatory risk in the West. It won't move today's price, but it compounds into long-term policy uncertainty. For swing traders, flag this as background noise; for HODLers, it's one more headwind on Western mining viability.

WATCH LIST

Bitcoin needs to hold $75,775 (24h low) to avoid testing deeper support around $74,000–$73,000. A retest of the $77,498 high would confirm profit-taking is done; a break below the low signals more pain ahead. Ethereum's underperformance relative to Bitcoin (-2.20% vs -2.10%) is worth monitoring—if altcoin weakness continues, expect more dominance flowing back to BTC. Stablecoin circulation at $256.8B is your canary in the coal mine; any sustained outflow without fresh buying pressure means conviction is fading. The next 24–48 hours are setup hours; big moves come when one of these supports breaks or holds decisively.

See you tomorrow — stay sharp, stack the dips, and don't chase shorts into a bid wall.
